title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Studies the chemical processes that govern air, water, soil, sediments, climate systems, and contaminants—integrating equilibrium, kinetics, redox, speciation, partitioning, atmospheric chemistry, nutrient cycles, contaminant fate, analytical QA/QC, treatment, green chemistry, and decision-oriented case analysis.

topics.title: Environmental Chemical Systems, Units, Mass Balance, and Thermodynamics
topics.description: Students learn to treat air, water, soils, sediments, and biota as coupled chemical systems governed by mass, energy, and equilibrium constraints.

children.title: Environmental compartments
children.description: The point is to see chemical behavior across connected reservoirs rather than isolated beakers.

children.title: Mass balance
children.description: Mass balance gives students a disciplined way to track sources, sinks, accumulation, and transport.

children.title: Thermodynamic foundations
children.description: Environmental reactions are constrained by energy, activity, and equilibrium.

topics.title: Aquatic Equilibria, Acid-Base Chemistry, and Alkalinity
topics.description: This module develops the equilibrium tools used to interpret natural waters, wastewater, oceans, and acidification.

children.title: Acid-base systems
children.description: Natural-water pH is controlled by weak acids, bases, buffering, and gas exchange.

children.title: Alkalinity
children.description: Alkalinity is a practical measure of acid-neutralizing capacity and water-system resilience.

children.title: Equilibrium modeling
children.description: Students learn to solve water chemistry problems quantitatively.

topics.title: Carbonate System, Ocean Acidification, and Climate-Relevant Aqueous Chemistry
topics.description: Students study carbonate chemistry as a master variable for pH, alkalinity, buffering, and carbon cycling.

children.title: Carbonate equilibria
children.description: Carbonate chemistry links atmospheric CO2 to water pH and mineral stability.

children.title: Ocean acidification
children.description: Students connect chemical shifts to ecological and geochemical consequences.

children.title: Carbon accounting in waters
children.description: Carbon measurements require careful distinction among related quantities.

topics.title: Redox Chemistry in Natural and Engineered Environments
topics.description: This topic explains how electron-transfer conditions control metals, nutrients, contaminants, and microbial processes.

children.title: Redox potential
children.description: Redox conditions determine which species are stable and mobile.

children.title: Environmental redox sequences
children.description: Microbial and chemical processes consume electron acceptors in predictable order.

children.title: Oxygen, nitrate, manganese, iron, sulfate, and methane zones
Redox transformations
children.description: Many contaminants and nutrients change fate when oxidized or reduced.

topics.title: Metal Speciation, Complexation, Toxicity, and Bioavailability
topics.description: Students learn that total concentration is rarely enough; chemical form controls mobility, toxicity, and treatment.

children.title: Speciation
children.description: Chemical form controls solubility, transport, and biological uptake.

children.title: Complexation and ligands
children.description: Natural and synthetic ligands can mobilize or immobilize metals.

children.title: Bioavailability and toxicity
children.description: Risk depends on exposure to biologically active forms, not just total metal concentration.

topics.title: Sorption, Partitioning, Interfaces, Soils, and Sediments
topics.description: This module connects molecular interactions at surfaces to contaminant fate in terrestrial and aquatic systems.

children.title: Sorption mechanisms
children.description: Surfaces control contaminant retention and release.

children.title: Partitioning
children.description: Organic compounds distribute among water, air, solids, and biota according to molecular properties.

children.title: Soil and sediment chemistry
children.description: Soils and sediments are reactive chemical matrices, not inert storage bins.

topics.title: Atmospheric Composition, Photochemistry, Radicals, and Ozone
topics.description: Students learn how sunlight and reactive species drive atmospheric transformation and air quality.

children.title: Atmospheric composition
children.description: Students learn the chemical baseline of the atmosphere and why trace gases matter.

children.title: Photochemistry and radicals
children.description: Sunlight initiates radical chains that transform pollutants and control oxidizing capacity.

children.title: Ozone chemistry
children.description: Ozone is protective in the stratosphere and harmful in the troposphere.

topics.title: Aerosols, Particulate Matter, Deposition, and Atmospheric-Water Coupling
topics.description: This topic covers particles and deposition as chemical links among air, water, soil, ecosystems, and health.

children.title: Aerosol formation
children.description: Particles form directly from emissions or through gas-to-particle conversion.

children.title: Particle properties and impacts
children.description: Particle size and composition determine transport, visibility, climate, and health effects.

children.title: Deposition and cloud chemistry
children.description: Atmospheric chemistry returns to surfaces through wet and dry deposition.

topics.title: Nutrient Chemistry, Eutrophication, and Biogeochemical Cycles
topics.description: Students study nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur, carbon, and trace elements as cycling chemical networks.

children.title: Nitrogen chemistry
children.description: Nitrogen changes oxidation state and mobility through biological and chemical pathways.

children.title: Phosphorus chemistry
children.description: Phosphorus often limits aquatic productivity and is strongly controlled by sorption and precipitation.

children.title: Eutrophication and cycles
children.description: Nutrient enrichment links chemistry to ecosystem response.

children.title: Carbon, sulfur, and trace nutrient cycles

topics.title: Organic Contaminant Fate, Transport, and Transformation
topics.description: This module develops environmental organic chemistry for pollutants, pesticides, solvents, fuels, and natural organic matter.

children.title: Molecular properties
children.description: Chemical structure helps predict persistence, volatility, solubility, and partitioning.

children.title: Transport and fate
children.description: Organic contaminants move and transform through coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes.

children.title: Transformation pathways
children.description: Environmental reactions can detoxify compounds or create harmful products.

topics.title: Emerging Contaminants, PFAS, Microplastics, and Chemical Risk
topics.description: Students examine modern contaminant classes and why persistence, exposure, and uncertainty make them difficult.

children.title: PFAS chemistry
children.description: PFAS illustrate persistence, mobility, and analytical difficulty in modern environmental chemistry.

children.title: Microplastics and additives
children.description: Plastic particles and additives create physical and chemical exposure questions.

children.title: Risk framing
children.description: Students learn to connect hazard, exposure, uncertainty, and decision-making.

topics.title: Environmental Analytical Methods, Sampling, QA/QC, and Data Interpretation
topics.description: This topic teaches how environmental chemistry evidence is generated, validated, and interpreted.

children.title: Sampling design
children.description: Environmental data are only as good as the field strategy behind them.

children.title: Analytical methods
children.description: Students learn which measurements reveal which chemical forms and why method choice matters.

children.title: QA/QC and interpretation
children.description: Quality controls make environmental claims defensible.

topics.title: Treatment, Remediation, and Green Chemistry Technologies
topics.description: Students connect chemistry to engineered interventions that prevent, remove, transform, or immobilize contaminants.

children.title: Water and wastewater treatment chemistry
children.description: Treatment processes manipulate chemistry to remove or transform contaminants.

children.title: Remediation
children.description: Contaminated sites require chemical strategies matched to contaminant and matrix.

children.title: Green chemistry
children.description: Prevention is often better than cleanup, so students learn safer chemical design.

topics.title: Climate Chemistry, Greenhouse Gases, and Earth-System Feedbacks
topics.description: This module links molecular chemistry to climate forcing, feedbacks, and environmental change.

children.title: Greenhouse gases
children.description: Molecular absorption properties determine radiative forcing.

children.title: Climate feedback chemistry
children.description: Chemical processes feed back into warming, air quality, and ecosystems.

children.title: Climate mitigation chemistry
children.description: Chemistry is central to emissions reduction and carbon management.

topics.title: Environmental Chemistry Case Study and Field-to-Policy Project
topics.description: The course culminates in a rigorous case analysis connecting field data, chemical mechanisms, uncertainty, impacts, and decisions.

children.title: Case framing
children.description: Students define a real environmental chemistry problem with stakeholders, mechanisms, and evidence needs.

children.title: Data and mechanism synthesis
children.description: The project integrates chemical calculations, field or public data, and uncertainty.

children.title: Communication and decision support
children.description: High-quality work explains chemistry clearly enough to support action.
